questions.prompt: In what order does a PLC do the steps of one scan?
options: Read the inputs, run the program, write the outputs, housekeeping
Run the program, read the inputs, write the outputs, housekeeping
Write the outputs, read the inputs, run the program, housekeeping
Read the inputs and write the outputs at once, then run the program
questions.explanation: The program works on a snapshot of the inputs, and its results go out together at the end.

questions.prompt: In PLC+ one scan is 10 ms. How many scans run in one second?
questions.explanation: 1 s = 1000 ms, and 1000 ms / 10 ms = 100 scans.

questions.prompt: Rung 1 is Start → Motor. Rung 5 is Jog → Motor. Start is pressed and Jog is not. What does the motor do?
options: It stays off: rung 5 runs later and turns Motor off again in the same scan
It runs: rung 1 turned it on
It flickers on and off every scan
The PLC stops with a fault
questions.explanation: Two coils of one tag is the double coil mistake: the later rung overwrites the earlier one, and only the last value is written out.

questions.prompt: The scan is 10 ms. A sensor turns on for 3 ms between two reads of the inputs. What does the program see?
options: Nothing: the pulse came and went between two reads
questions.explanation: Inputs are read once per scan. A pulse shorter than a scan can fall between two reads and be missed.

questions.prompt: A button is pressed while the processor is working on rung 10 of 20. When does rung 3 see it?
options: In the next scan, after the inputs are read again
questions.explanation: The inputs are copied once, at the start of each scan. Every rung in one scan sees the same snapshot.
